ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
There is a crane with a maximum power of $P_{m}=8{\times}10^{3}\mathrm{W}$, lifting an object with a mass of $m=1000\mathrm{kg}$ vertically upward. Neglecting air resistance, the gravitational acceleration is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What is the maximum speed that the object can ultimately reach if the crane operates at maximum power?
2. If the object is rising at a constant speed of $v=0.4\mathrm{m/s}$, what is the actual power of the crane?
3. If an object accelerates upward from rest with an acceleration of $a=2\mathbf{m}/\mathbf{s}^{2}$, how long can this acceleration be maintained?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: There is a crane with a maximum power of $P_{m}=8{\times}10^{3}\mathrm{W}$, lifting an object with a mass of $m=1000\mathrm{kg}$ vertically upward. Neglecting air resistance, the gravitational acceleration is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. 1. What is the maximum speed that the object can ultimately reach if the crane operates at maximum power? 2. If the object is rising at a constant speed of $v=0.4\mathrm{m/s}$, what is the actual power of the crane? 3. If an object accelerates upward from rest with an acceleration of $a=2\mathbf{m}/\mathbf{s}^{2}$, how long can this acceleration be maintained?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given P_m = 8.0×10^3 W, m = 1000 kg, g = 10 m/s^2. 1) The ultimate maximum speed occurs when the object is no longer accelerating, so the crane force only balances weight: F = mg = 1000×10 = 10000 N. Using P = Fv at maximum power, v_max = P_m/(mg) = 8000/10000 = 0.8 m/s. 2) At constant speed v = 0.4 m/s, acceleration is zero, so F = mg. The actual power is P = mgv = 1000×10×0.4 = 4000 W. 3) For upward acceleration a = 2 m/s^2 from rest, the required crane force is F = m(g+a) = 1000×(10+2) = 12000 N. During constant acceleration, v = at = 2t. The required power is P = Fv = 12000×2t = 24000t. Setting this equal to the maximum power 8000 W gives 24000t = 8000, so t = 1/3 s.
